questions.text: What's it for? The 1.87 mm section, 2.8× slenderness, and small 90° ceiling are consistent with several roles; the shape alone can't say which.

options.label: Functional (holds, clips, or bears load)
options.impact: Stronger core and walls; the 1.87 mm section gets 3 perimeters before infill, so walls carry most of the load. Slightly more material.

options.label: Decorative (a face shows)
options.impact: Lighter, faster; the 138 mm² flat top is where finish lives, so top layers matter more than infill. Less structural margin.

options.label: Prototype (check fit or shape)
options.impact: Preset values; no reason to spend extra material on a throwaway.

questions.text: The 90° ceiling (10 mm²) — a small horizontal face pointing straight down, the steepest overhang in the part.

options.label: Bridge, no support
options.impact: Fastest, clean surface under the ceiling. At 10 mm² the span is short (the whole part is 16 × 8 mm), so it should hold at 0.2 mm layers with the preset's fan. Risk: a slight sag if the span runs in a weak direction.
options.why: Ten square millimetres on a 16 × 8 mm part is a very short span — at most a few millimetres. At 0.2 mm layer height with the preset's cooling, that will bridge cleanly. Tree support for a face this small introduces more surface artifacts (contact points, removal marks) than the bridge risk warrants.

options.label: Tree support
options.impact: Guaranteed flat ceiling. Support marks on a 10 mm² area are easy to remove. Slightly longer print.

options.label: Design note: chamfer the edge to 45°
options.impact: Eliminates the overhang entirely; the part prints with no special handling. This is a CAD change, not a slicer setting.
